issue.zero.headline: This magazine grows out of whatever you play.
issue.zero.cadence: At the start of every month, the month just gone becomes an issue: a cover story, the rankings, the superlatives, the artists you heard for the first time. Not a once-a-year campaign, and nothing for you to do.
issue.zero.honesty: The editor's note is assembled from real numbers only — not a word of it is invented. Where the data cannot carry a sentence, that sentence never appears.
issue.zero.privacy: Your listening history never leaves this device. Take it with you as JSON or CSV whenever you like; the taste profile behind the recommendations is laid out in the open, and any part of it can be switched off on the spot.

settings.replayGain.name: Volume levelling · ReplayGain
settings.replayGain.desc: Reads the gain the server already computed, so masters from different eras sit at the same loudness. “Auto” keeps an album's own dynamics when you play it in order, and levels track by track on shuffle.
settings.replayGain.label: Volume levelling

settings.notificationActions.desc: Which two buttons sit on the lock screen and system media panel. Music wants previous and next; audiobooks want skip back and forward — one panel cannot serve both

settings.seekStep.desc: How many seconds those two lock-screen buttons jump
settings.carMode.desc: Oversized targets, swipe to change track, screen stays awake. Also under “More” on mobile, or press ⇧C on desktop

settings.musicBrainz.name: Fill in from MusicBrainz
settings.musicBrainz.desc: Formation year, where they are from, the line-up, the official site — none of that lives in audio tags. When on, opening an artist page sends that artist's MusicBrainz id to musicbrainz.org; your account, library and listening history are never sent. Off by default.
